title: Dynamic tone mapping and density-aware shadow presets for forms & tables
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our current token set has static color ramps and a single shadow/elevation scale that do not adapt well to high-density UIs (compact tables/forms) or variable background tones (cards vs. surfaces). This causes inconsistent perceived elevation and failing contrast in condensed layouts.

Goal: Introduce a set of dynamic tone-mapping tokens and density-aware shadow presets so components can pick appropriate color ramps and elevation shadows based on density and surface context. The work should be backward-compatible with the existing token aliases and include migration guidance for component owners.

Scope: color tone ramps for primary/neutral/accent with light/dark modulation, a density token (compact/comfortable/expanded), three shadow presets per density level tuned for common component sizes (controls, cards, data rows), and developer-facing utilities (SCSS mixins / CSS variables / Figma tokens) for live-preview and QA.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens defined: tone-map-primary-{light|neutral|dark}, tone-map-neutral-{light|neutral|dark}, density-{compact|comfortable|expanded}, shadow-{density}-{level1|level2|level3}
Figma library updated with token variants and interactive examples for forms, tables, dropdowns, and cards
Contrast verification: all foreground/background combinations for primary and neutral ramps meet 4.5:1 for body text and 3:1 for UI elements in compact density
QA harness in Storybook shows components switching tokens based on density control and surface tone selector
Migration guide published with mapping from legacy tokens to the new tone/density tokens and a phased rollout plan
No visual regressions for flagship pages (dashboard table, settings form) beyond approved design deltas
design_notes: Tone mapping is modeled as a pair of variables: --tone-surface (background anchor) and --tone-accent (color ramp anchor). Components compute color by combining base ramp with surface anchor to preserve contrast on tonal surfaces.

Density token is an explicit prop that flows from Console settings and can be overridden per component (default comfortable). We will provide CSS utilities to scope density to sections (e.g., compact table rows inside a dense panel).

Shadow presets are redesigned to prioritize blur and subtle vertical offset over heavy spread to avoid visual noise in compact rows. Each density has three levels: subtle (hover), medium (layer), pronounced (modal).
We will keep existing token aliases (e.g., color-bg-surface, color-text-primary) and map them to new computed tokens to reduce churn for engineers.
Edge case: charts use high-contrast stroke colors and should not receive tone mapping that reduces legibility; charts will opt out by default and use explicit chart tokens.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize token names and Figma examples; publish token spec in Confluence with live palettes and contrast matrices
Phase 2 (Platform): land CSS variables and SCSS mixins in component library under a feature flag; add Storybook knobs for density and surface tone
Phase 3 (Component owners): update components to consume new tokens via aliases; test with QA harness and fix regressions
Phase 4 (Rollout): enable feature flag for a small set of pages (dashboard list, user settings), monitor visual diffs and accessibility metrics, then ramp to all surfaces
Mapping snippet: legacy color-bg-surface -> var(--tone-surface-neutral), legacy color-text-primary -> color-from(var(--tone-accent), 700)
rollout_plan: Week 1: Publish token spec and Figma library; announce to engineering and product teams with migration guidelines
Week 2: Implement variables & utilities in main CSS package behind feature flag; ship Storybook examples
Week 3-4: Coordinate with 3 component owners (Table, Form, Card) to adopt tokens and run visual regression tests
Week 5: Enable on staging for smoke-tests and accessibility scan; gather feedback from design review
Week 6: Gradual production ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with fallback to legacy tokens via runtime flag if regressions detected
qa_checks: Automated visual diffs for dashboard table and settings form across densities (compact/comfortable/expanded)
Contrast scan report for all token permutations against WCAG 2.1 AA requirements
Manual review checklist for spacing and overlap in compact density (row height, hit targets, icon alignment)
Performance sniff: ensure no noticeable repaint jank when switching density or surface tone in Storybook
Cross-browser validation (Chromium-based, Firefox, Safari) for CSS variable fallbacks
accessibility_checks: All text >= 14px must meet 4.5:1 contrast against computed background tokens in compact density
UI icons and small controls must meet 3:1 contrast or have accessible labels
Keyboard focus shadows must remain visible in compact mode; provide higher-contrast focus token if necessary
Screen-reader announcements unaffected; density is presentation-only and must not break DOM order
